probe_note_worth_keeping.our_words: The first in-page search for 'Article 25' returned NOT FOUND on a document that plainly contains it. The separator is a non-breaking space (U+00A0), not a space. A plain indexOf on EUR-Lex article headings gives a false absence.
probe_note_worth_keeping.consequence: Any future gate or probe that greps EUR-Lex rendered text for an article heading must allow \s\u00a0 between the word and the number, or it will report a live article as missing.

article_25.heading_as_stated: Article 25 — Online interface design and organisation

paragraph_1.our_words: Providers of online platforms are forbidden to design, organise or run their interfaces so as to deceive or manipulate users, or otherwise to materially distort or impair users' ability to make free and informed decisions.
paragraph_1.receipt: "shall not design, organise or operate their online interfaces in a way that deceives"
paragraph_1.note_our_words: The prohibition has TWO limbs, not one: deception/manipulation, AND material distortion or impairment of free and informed decision-making. The second limb is broader and does not require intent to deceive.

paragraph_2.our_words: The paragraph-1 prohibition does not apply to practices already covered by the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive (2005/29/EC) or by the GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679).
paragraph_2.receipt: "The prohibition in paragraph 1 shall not apply to practices covered by Directive 2005/29/EC"
paragraph_2.note_our_words: This is a carve-out that routes a practice to whichever instrument already governs it, so Article 25 is a residual prohibition rather than an overlapping one. The register's existing scope_conditions on pr-dsa25 ('Overlaps with, and defers to, GDPR and consumer law') is CORRECT and is now sourced.

paragraph_3.our_words: The Commission may issue guidelines on how paragraph 1 applies to specific practices, and the Article names three examples: giving more prominence to certain choices; repeatedly re-asking a choice already made, especially via pop-ups that interfere with the experience; and making cancellation harder than sign-up.
paragraph_3.receipt: "The Commission may issue guidelines on how paragraph 1 applies to specific practices"
named_examples_our_words: (a) weighting one choice more prominently than another when asking for a decision
(b) asking again for a choice already made, especially with interfering pop-ups
paragraph_3.note_our_words: These three are the only practices the Article itself names, and all three are design decisions a generator makes. (a) is visual weight, (b) is interruption, (c) is flow length.
